artifacts.name: About this indicator
artifacts.summary: Maps swimming pools in the area and separates publicly accessible bathing sites from private garden pools. Public pools are important heat refuges, and the split between public and private pools is a lens on who can cool down and how.

artifacts.name: Density distribution
artifacts.summary: How swimming pools density varies across neighbourhoods, as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.75; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
The distribution of swimming pools density (per km²) across the area’s administrative sub-areas, shown as a Lorenz curve (Gini 0.75; 0 = perfectly even, 1 = all in one sub-area). A long tail or low median points to many under-served neighbourhoods.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Statistics
artifacts.summary: Spread, inequality and clustering measures for the area’s swimming pools. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description: Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Hot-spots & cold-spots
artifacts.summary: Global Moran’s I = -0.25. 0 hot-spot and 0 cold-spot neighbourhood(s) of swimming pools density (local Moran’s I / LISA). Only 10 sub-areas: too few for the permutation test to establish significance, so read a grey map as "not enough units to tell", not as "no clustering". Use a finer `subarea_mode` or a larger area to make this map informative. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Sub-areas classified by the local Moran’s I statistic (LISA) over swimming pools density: **High-High** = a dense neighbourhood surrounded by others like it (hot-spot); **Low-Low** = a sparse one among others like it (cold-spot); **High-Low / Low-High** = spatial outliers. Significance uses a deterministic permutation test; non-significant sub-areas are greyed out.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision vs population
artifacts.summary: Do swimming pools track where people live? Swimming pools per 1,000 inhabitants against each sub-area’s population. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each point is an administrative sub-area, plotting its population against its swimming pools per 1,000 inhabitants. Sub-areas low on the vertical axis but high on the horizontal axis are under-served relative to their residents — an equity signal a density map cannot show.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Provision per capita
artifacts.summary: Swimming pools per 1,000 residents across the sub-areas — provision relative to need. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
Each administrative sub-area shaded by its number of swimming pools per 1,000 inhabitants, so the colour reflects provision *relative to residents* rather than raw density. A populous sub-area with average density can still read as under-served here. Sub-areas without usable population data are omitted.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.description:
The area of interest split into the part within reach (on foot) of any feature and the part beyond it. Reachability is computed using straight-line distance.

Each administrative sub-area shaded by the fraction of its area that lies **beyond reach** (on foot) of any feature — the complement of the coverage map. Darker = more underserved. Use it to target where new provision would reach the most currently-unserved people.

A kernel-smoothed density of swimming pools: the point counts are blurred into a continuous surface so clusters show as smooth hot regions rather than individual grid cells — a boundary-free complement to the sub-area choropleth and the raw heatmap.

artifacts.name: Distance to nearest swimming pool
artifacts.summary: How far to the nearest swimming pool from anywhere in the area (metres). Darker = further. Results depend on OpenStreetMap data completeness. If you can, contribute to OSM.
artifacts.description:
A regular grid over the area, each cell shaded by the straight-line distance to the nearest swimming pool. Dark cells are the furthest from any feature — the access gaps. Straight-line (not routed), so it is an optimistic lower bound; it needs no routing service.

Provenance: OpenStreetMap data as of 2026-06-19 · indicator: swimming_pools · reachability: straight-line distance.

artifacts.name: Data currentness

artifacts.description:
Each point is a feature, shaded by the number of years since its last OpenStreetMap edit (measured against the data snapshot). Clusters of dark points mark areas where the OSM picture is ageing and may warrant a re-survey — a spatial companion to the data-quality note.
